candidates.title: Robust and Computationally Efficient Linear Contextual Bandits under Adversarial Corruption and Heavy-Tailed Noise
candidates.source_citation: arXiv:2603.15596: 'We study linear contextual bandits under adversarial corruption and heavy-tailed noise with finite $(1+\epsilon)$-th moments for some $\epsilon\in (0,1]$. Existing work that addresses both adversarial corruption and heavy-tailed noise relies on a finite variance (i.e., finite second-moment) assumption and suffers from computational inefficiency.'
candidates.claimed_gap: Existing work relies on finite variance assumptions and suffers from computational inefficiency under simultaneous adversarial corruption and heavy-tailed noise with finite (1+eps)-th moments.

candidates.title: Online Learning of Whittle Indices for Restless Bandits with Non-Stationary Transition Kernels
candidates.source_citation: arXiv:2506.18186: 'This paper introduced an online/reinforcement learning algorithm for estimating the Whittle index for restless bandit problems with unknown and non-stationary transition kernels using sliding window and upper confidence bound approaches.'
candidates.claimed_gap: Whittle index policies require access to stationary transition kernels - an unrealistic assumption in many networked systems, demanding sliding window and UCB adaptations for non-stationary dynamics.
